description: A C# game engine in which a program opens a window, draws each frame with plain static calls named as raylib's functions are, and draws Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
A device that draws on its CPU takes no samples along a slant, since lavapipe's sixteen blurred a texture drawn at its own size and put the captures job's pairs past their rooms.
Core names no area above it, DefaultPlugins composed in Api, the window's size and the renderer's state read through interfaces of Core, and picking a plugin of its own.
The path-traced reference reads each copy's texture and normal map at the point it meets, through texture coordinates the ray scene keeps and an array of textures the device indexes per ray.
The console's gi.toggle normals off lights every face by its own normal for a reading, with global illumination on or off, and RENDERING.md records Sponza's grazed faces read so.
RENDERING.md records the pocket mark at 16 by 16 and four rays a texel in High's first two cascades, neither landed since the canopy's floor and the metal walls leave their bounds at that size.
The comments of the sources, shaders, scripts and workflows explain the code in the engine's own terms, with no other product's profile, outside asset's file name, sibling's reading or run of the work as the reason, and STYLE.md says so with its search.
The device maps a memory block once a buffer the CPU writes is carved from it, which mends the scene field pool's null copy on lavapipe, and the middle dot leaves the samples, the comments and the README.
A carried probe keeps its share of the sky and its mark of what its rays met over the cycle of places its rays move through as it keeps its light, which stills the flicker of Sponza's edges held still, and build/flicker.py reads a recording picture to picture for the share of the pixels that moved.
title: 3DEngine
